source_refs.note: Chapter 8 exercise (PDF 185-188), solved: 11 MCQs keyed from the chapter (no key is printed) and 11 short questions with model answers; j (Qc) and k (equilibrium concentration) worked step by step. MCQ II and short j carry Book corrections.

blocks.text: Q.1 Four choices are given for each question. Select the correct choice.

blocks.prompt: I. For which system, does the equilibrium constant, Kc has units of (concentration)⁻¹?

options.text: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃
H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI
2NO₂ ⇌ N₂O₄
2HF ⇌ H₂ + F₂

blocks.explanation: Units of Kc = (concentration)^Δn, Δn = moles of products − moles of reactants. For 2NO₂ ⇌ N₂O₄, Δn = 1 − 2 = −1, so Kc = [N₂O₄]/[NO₂]² has units (mol dm⁻³)⁻¹. (a) has Δn = −2 (units mol⁻² dm⁶); (b) and (d) have Δn = 0 (no units) (8.8.2).

blocks.prompt:
II. Which statement about the following equilibrium is correct?
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)  ∆H = −197.9 kJ mol⁻¹

options.text: The value of Kp falls with a rise in temperature.
The value of Kp falls with increasing pressure.
Adding V₂O₅ catalyst increase the equilibrium yield of sulphur trioxide.
The value of Kp is equal to Kc.

blocks.explanation: The forward reaction is exothermic, so a rise in temperature favours the reverse reaction and the equilibrium constant falls (8.14). Pressure changes the position, not Kp; a catalyst does not change the yield (8.15); Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn with Δn = −1, so Kp ≠ Kc.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Option (c) is printed 'Adding V₂O₅ catalyst increase'; it reads 'increases'. In the book the word 'EXERCISE' is printed after this question instead of before the MCQs.

blocks.prompt:
III. 2SO₃(g) ⇌ 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g)
The conventional equilibrium constant expression (Kc) for the system as described by the above equation is:

options.text: [SO₂]²/[SO₃]
[SO₂]²[O₂]/[SO₃]²
[SO₃]²/[SO₃]²[O₂]
[SO₂][O₂]

blocks.explanation: Kc = products raised to their coefficients over reactants raised to their coefficients: Kc = [SO₂]²[O₂]/[SO₃]² (8.8).

blocks.prompt: IV. A saturated solution represents a dynamic equilibrium. Macroscopically, the concentration of dissolved solute is constant. Microscopically, this occurs because:

options.text: No more solute particles are dissolving.
The rate of dissolution of solute is zero.
Solute particles are dissolving and precipitating at the same rate.
All solute particles have dissolved.

blocks.explanation: At dynamic equilibrium both opposite processes continue at equal rates, so no net change is seen (8.2, 8.4).

blocks.prompt: V. Which of the following statements correctly describes the effect of temperature on the equilibrium constant?

options.text: Kc is directly proportional to temperature.
Kc is inversely proportional to temperature.
Kc depends on the enthalpy change of the reaction.
Temperature has no effect on the value of Kc.

blocks.explanation: Temperature is the only factor that changes Kc, and the direction depends on ΔH: for an exothermic reaction Kc decreases on heating, for an endothermic reaction it increases (8.14). So it is neither simply directly nor inversely proportional.

blocks.prompt:
VI. Consider the gas-phase equilibrium system represented by the equation:
2H₂O(g) ⇌ 2H₂(g) + O₂(g)
Given that the forward reaction is endothermic, which of the following changes will decrease the equilibrium amount of H₂O?

options.text: Adding more oxygen
Adding a solid phase catalyst
Decreasing the volume of the container (the total pressure increases)
Increasing the temperature at constant pressure

blocks.explanation: For an endothermic forward reaction, heating favours the forward reaction, so H₂O is used up (8.14). Adding O₂ and decreasing the volume (3 mol gas → 2 mol gas on the left) shift the equilibrium to the left and increase H₂O; a catalyst has no effect on the amounts.

blocks.prompt:
VII. Kc = 0.040 for the reaction given below at 450 °C:
PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g)
Evaluate Kp for the reaction at 450 °C.
VIII. In which of the following gaseous equilibria, pressure has no effect on the equilibrium position?

options.text: 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g)
PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g)
CO(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO₂(g) + H₂(g)
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)

blocks.explanation: Pressure has no effect when the moles of gaseous reactants and products are equal (8.13). In (c) there are 2 mol of gas on each side.

blocks.prompt: IX. Consider the equilibrium 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2H₂O(g). If the concentration of H₂O(g) is increased, the concentrations of H₂(g) and O₂(g) will:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Remain the same.
Change irregularly

blocks.explanation: Adding a product shifts the equilibrium in the reverse direction (Le Chatelier's principle, 8.12), so some H₂O breaks down and the concentrations of H₂ and O₂ increase.

blocks.prompt: X. For a specific reaction, the value of the equilibrium constant, Kc:

options.text: always remains the same at different reaction conditions.
increases if the concentration of one of the products is increased.
changes with changes in the temperature.
increases if the concentration of one of the reactants is increased.

blocks.explanation: Kc does not depend on concentrations; it depends on temperature only (8.6, 8.14). Changing a concentration only shifts the position.

blocks.prompt: XI. For a saturated solution of a salt in water, a dynamic equilibrium is between:

options.text: The dissolved ions and the undissolved solid salt
The solute and the solvent molecules
The solid salt and the water molecules
The hydrated ions and the water molecules in the bulk solvent

blocks.explanation: Ions leave the solid (dissolve) and ions from the solution return to the solid (crystallize) at the same rate: solid ⇌ dissolved ions.

blocks.text: Q.2 Attempt the following short-answer questions:

blocks.prompt: a. What is meant by the state of chemical equilibrium?
blocks.explanation: The state of a reversible reaction at which the composition of the reaction mixture does not change and the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal. The concentrations of reactants and products then stay constant (8.2).

blocks.prompt: b. Define reversible reaction. Give an example.
blocks.explanation:
A reaction that proceeds in both directions, forward and reverse, so that the products react to give back the reactants; in a closed vessel it never goes to completion and reaches equilibrium (8.1).
Example: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)

blocks.prompt:
c. Decide the comparative magnitudes of Kc and Kp, for the following reversible reactions.
(i) Ammonia synthesis (ii) Dissociation of PCl₅
blocks.explanation:
Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn, and RT > 1 (R = 0.0821 dm³ atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, T in K) (8.9).
(i) N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃: Δn = 2 − 4 = −2, Kp = Kc/(RT)², so Kp < Kc.
(ii) PCl₅ ⇌ PCl₃ + Cl₂: Δn = 2 − 1 = +1, Kp = Kc(RT), so Kp > Kc.

blocks.prompt: d. The change of volume disturbs the equilibrium position for some of the gas phase reactions but not the equilibrium constant.
blocks.explanation: Changing the volume changes all gas concentrations at once. If the moles of gas differ on the two sides (Δn ≠ 0), the ratio Qc no longer equals Kc, so the reaction shifts (to fewer moles when volume decreases) until the ratio again equals the same Kc. Kc itself depends only on temperature, so it does not change; if Δn = 0, the position is not disturbed at all (8.13).

blocks.prompt: e. Mention the characteristics of chemical equilibrium.
blocks.explanation:
1. Concentrations of reactants and products remain constant; forward and reverse rates are equal (dynamic).
2. It can be approached from either side, starting with reactants or products.
3. A catalyst does not change the equilibrium position or K; it only helps to reach equilibrium earlier.
4. K does not depend on initial concentrations; it depends on temperature only. It is set up only in a closed system (8.5, 8.6).

blocks.prompt: f. Reversible reaction attains the position of equilibrium which is dynamic in nature and not static. Explain it.
blocks.explanation: At equilibrium the concentrations stop changing, so the reaction seems to have stopped (static). But at the microscopic level reactant molecules keep reacting to form products and product molecules keep reacting to form reactants; both reactions continue at equal rates, so there is no net change. E.g. in H₂O(g) + CO(g) ⇌ H₂(g) + CO₂(g) bonds keep breaking and forming in both directions (8.2).

blocks.prompt: g. Why do the rates of forward reactions slow down when a reversible reaction approaches the equilibrium stage?
blocks.explanation: The forward rate depends on the concentrations of reactants. As reactants are used up, their concentrations fall, so there are fewer collisions per second between them and the forward rate decreases; at the same time products build up and the reverse rate increases until the two rates become equal (8.2).

blocks.prompt: h. Why ice at 0 °C can be melted by applying pressure without supply of heat from outside?
blocks.explanation: At 0 °C ice and water are in dynamic equilibrium: ice ⇌ water. Ice occupies more volume than the same mass of water (about 9% more). By Le Chatelier's principle, increased pressure favours the change that decreases volume, so the equilibrium shifts towards water and the ice melts. Pressure lowers the melting point below 0 °C; the heat for melting comes from the ice-water system itself, whose temperature falls slightly (beyond the chapter).

blocks.prompt: i. Write two conditions of equilibrium constant.
blocks.explanation:
1. The reaction must be reversible and must have reached equilibrium; the concentrations put into Kc are equilibrium concentrations.
2. The system must be closed, so that no reactant or product escapes, and the temperature must be constant, because Kc changes only with temperature (8.5, 8.6).

blocks.prompt:
j. At 445 °C, Kc for the following reaction is 0.020.
2HI(g) ⇌ H₂(g) + I₂(g)
A mixture of H₂, I₂, and HI in a vessel at 445 °C has the following concentrations: [HI] = 2.0 M, [H₂] = 0.50 M and [I₂] = 0.10 M. Which one of the following statements concerning the reaction quotient, Qc, is TRUE for the above system?
i) Qc = Kc; the system is at equilibrium.
ii) Qc is less than Kc; more H₂ and I₂ will be produced.
iii) Qc is less than Kc; more HI will be produced.
iv) Qc is greater than Kc; more H₂ and I₂ will be produced.
blocks.explanation:
Given: Kc = 0.020, [HI] = 2.0 M, [H₂] = 0.50 M, [I₂] = 0.10 M
Qc = [H₂][I₂] / [HI]²
Qc = (0.50 × 0.10) / (2.0)² = 0.050 / 4.0
Qc = 0.0125
Qc (0.0125) < Kc (0.020), so the system is not at equilibrium; the forward reaction proceeds until Qc = Kc, producing more H₂ and I₂.
True statement: (ii)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The value of Kc is printed in Arabic-Indic (Urdu) numerals with a comma as the decimal sign; it reads 0.020, as written here.

blocks.prompt:
k. The reversible reaction:
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)
has come to equilibrium in a vessel of specific volume at a given temperature. Before the reaction began, the concentrations of the reactants were 0.060 mol/dm³ of SO₂ and 0.050 mol/dm³ of O₂. After equilibrium is reached, the concentration of SO₃ is 0.040 mol/dm³. What is the equilibrium concentration of O₂?
blocks.explanation:
2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (mole ratio 2 : 1 : 2)
Initial: SO₂ 0.060, O₂ 0.050, SO₃ 0 mol dm⁻³
SO₃ formed = 0.040 mol dm⁻³
O₂ used = ½ × 0.040 = 0.020 mol dm⁻³ (SO₂ used = 0.040 mol dm⁻³)
[O₂] at equilibrium = 0.050 − 0.020 = 0.030 mol dm⁻³
(also [SO₂] = 0.060 − 0.040 = 0.020 mol dm⁻³)
Answer: [O₂] = 0.030 mol/dm³
